why_trail.why: The blocker is one clause in two files, and the reviewer's measurement of it reproduces on inspection: skills/{implementer,reviewer}/SKILL.md:17 both name the "terminal provenance check — the lease must cover every journaled action", and neither crew plan template has a closeout gate, so the clause's "archive gate ... fails your own closeout" names the wrong check for the wrong reader. The repair is to use the inherited name and scope the release-and-rebind escape to the reader who actually faces it, then measure every assertion left standing.

The clause now says what is true for the reader of these two files: the escape is barred by the role's own doctrine, which holds the lease open until the last action because the lease must cover every journaled action — the inherited "terminal provenance check", named as skills/{implementer,reviewer}/SKILL.md:17 names it, not renamed into a gate. And the second half is scoped honestly: a crew dispatched without a spine arrives holding no lease, so the release-and-rebind escape never arises for it at all. "archive gate" is now absent from specs/ and skills/; both files parse, compile clean, and the guard reports no specs/ address (its only two failures are lane D2's fenced skills/workbench files, byte-identical to baseline).

Every assertion left standing in the added prose is now measured rather than restated: 51 checks in verify_claims.py (the repaired clause against both role skills' own wording, the dispatch env from run_crew._crew_door_env, the nine-tool inventory off the door's own schemas, the engine's symmetric advance/record refusal that makes the survey dialect real, the shared verbs exercised on both dialects with condition-kind isolated, the cited decision id, and the header comment's five compiler claims), plus 16 in door_probe.py across three fresh processes with a positive control. Two things the checks caught that prose review had not: both specs quoted the refusal as "release it first" where the door says "Release it first" (fixed in both; the probe now reads the quoted fragment out of the specs so it tracks the shipped text), and the launcher passes a dispatcher's own ambient SPINE_FILE/SPINE_SESSION through to a no-spine child, so "unbound" is a state the door reports rather than one to assume — the first engine run of this check failed for exactly that reason, and the probe now controls the ambient and measures both cases.

The result artifact is written and is the delivery: it quotes the clause before and after in both files, gives a measurement for every assertion left standing (not only the repaired one), records the two things the checks caught that prose review had not — the non-verbatim "release it first" quotation and the launcher's spine-pair pass-through — and states plainly what the clause deliberately does not claim, since the terminal provenance check is role doctrine with no live mechanical enforcement. Close criteria 1-8 all met; no stop condition was hit.
